title: South Street School

subtitle.text: Daisy: Jenna, it's finally here!
Jenna: Yay! Look, Daisy, I got a new
backpack. Daisy: Cool. I'm using my sister's old
one. But that's okay.
I like frogs.
Jenna: I can't wait to go back to South Street
School. And meet our teacher, Miss Gray.
It's such a nice name. It
rhymes with day, play, May . . . all great words! Daisy:
My sister said Miss Gray is really nice—and really pretty. Jenna:
I bet she lets us sit next to each other!
Come on! Let's run! Mark:
Ugh! It's the first day of school, Coby! Coby:
Don't remind me. Mark:
What's our teacher's name?
I keep forgetting.
Coby: And I keep telling you, Mark!
It's Miss Gray.
Mark: Oh, right. Gray, like a gloomy rain
cloud. Coby: Or a big, creepy
spider! Mark: Yuck! Second grade is going to be
awful! Coby: So who's your
teacher, Jenna? Jenna:
Miss Gray. Daisy: She's really nice and
really pretty. Mark: That's not what
we heard. We heard she’s
strange. Coby: Yep. And she looks like an alien
to me.
Jenna: What? Mr. Joe: Welcome
back, everyone. It's time to line up with your
class. Daisy: You two are
lying. Mark: Nope. We only tell the
truth. Jenna: Really? She looks like an
alien? Mr. Joe: Make a straight
line, kids. Here comes your teacher!
Kids: Huh?
Daisy: Is that really Miss Gray?
Coby: Yes. Why is she wearing a diving mask and fins?
Mark: I don't
know. But she looks
cool! Daisy: She doesn't look
cool. She looks
weird. Jenna: I don't believe
it. You were right,
Coby. She does look like an alien!
Miss Gray: Good morning, second
graders. Welcome back to South Street School. Follow
me, please! Mark: Where are
we going? Coby: Swimming, I
hope. Miss Gray: We're
going diving! In Room Two . . . Miss Gray:
We are going to dive into learning! Daisy: Dive
into learning? What does
that mean? Jenna: I
don't know what it means. But I
hate to swim. I'm probably going
to drown! Miss Gray:
Please go inside and find your seat. Mark: I
sit here. Look, Coby! You sit
next to me! Coby: Wow.
Second grade is going to be great! Jenna: I
found my name. Where
are you, Daisy? Daisy:
Oh no . . . I sit way over there, next to Kara. She's
so mean. I don't
want to sit next to her! Jenna: And I
have to sit next to two boys. Miss Gray:
Girls, you don't look happy. Is there
a problem? Jenna and
Daisy: No, Miss Gray. Miss Gray:
Good. Miss Gray:
Okay, boys and girls, now we're going to . . . Jenna:
Our teacher is Miss Gray .
I'm having a rotten day!
Mrs. Rock: How was your first day of school,
Coby? Coby: It was
great! Mrs. Rock: Great? This morning you didn't even want to
go. Coby: I know. But now I think second grade is
the best. Mrs.
Rock: Why? Coby: Miss
Gray is funny. And I sit
next to Mark. And guess what
else, Mom?
Mrs. Rock: What? Coby: Miss Gray
really likes sports. She said she'll play basketball at
recess with us. Mrs. Rock: Oh! Well, she does sound like
a fun teacher. Jenna: Hi,
Dad! Want some help? Mr. Gibson: Sure. Gibson Laundry
was very busy today. Mom and I worked hard
all day long. Mr. Gibson: So how was the first
day of school?
Jenna: It was terrible! Mr.
Gibson: Terrible? What happened? Jenna: I have to sit
next to two boys. And Miss Gray is
so . . . Mr.
Gibson: So what, honey? Jenna: So strange! This morning she had on
a diving mask and fins! Can
you believe that, Dad? And she kept saying we're going
to "dive into learning." Mr. Gibson: Oh. Well,
that sounds kind of interesting. Customer:
My son had Miss Gray.
She's a wonderful teacher, Jenna. Jenna:
Well, I still think she's
strange! Miss Gray: Yoo-hoo! I'm
home! There you are!
Come on, you two. It's time
to get ready. Tomorrow will be your first day of
school. And I've got big plans for you!
Mark: Second grade is the best!
Jenna and Daisy: Second grade is the
worst! Mr. Joe: Good morning, boys and
girls. Miss Gray is busy with something. So
I'm going to bring you to Room Two today. Coby: Hey,
is that a maze? Mark: I
think so. And
look! There are mice! Jenna: Did
somebody say mice ? Real mice? Jim:
Miss Gray, why are you wearing a stopwatch?
Miss Gray: Because Room Two is going to the races, Jim.
Class: What?
Miss Gray: Today we're diving into
math. That means we're going to do a fun math activity. Jenna:
The mice won't get hurt, will they?
Miss Gray: Of course not. They're just going to race.
Each mouse will run through the maze. We
will time them. Then we'll use
math to see which one is faster. Mark: Mouse math! Miss Gray:
On your
mark, get set . . . Class: Go! Miss Gray:
On your
mark, get set . . . Class: Go! Miss
Gray: Let’s
use mouse math now to compare them. Mark: The black
mouse took less time. So he won! Daisy: The
white mouse took twice as long. So she
lost. Miss Gray:
Good! Jenna: They're
cute. Do
they have names? Miss Gray:
That's Jill. And this is . . . Bill. Jenna: Hey,
that rhymes! Miss
Gray: Of course. I love rhyming words. Jenna:
Miss Gray? Can I tell you something? Miss
Gray: Sure, Jenna.
Jenna: I love Room Two.
I really do!
Miss Gray: Today we're going to learn about stars.
Daisy: Yay! I love movie
stars. Rock stars
too! Miss Gray: Not those kinds of stars,
Daisy. We're learning about stars in the sky. Daisy:
Oh . . .
Coby: Yes!
Mark: Twinkle, twinkle, little star . . .
Miss Gray: First, we're going to talk about stars.
Then, we're going to read about them. After
that, we're going to see them. Coby: See them?
How? Miss Gray: I'll
tell you more about that later. Now think
for a minute. What do you know
about stars? Coby: Ooh! Ooh! Stars are big
balls of hot gas! Miss Gray: Yes . .
. Coby: And the sun is
a star! Miss Gray: Jenna, do you
know anything about stars? Jenna: Stars rhymes with
bars, cars, jars. Miss Gray: True, but
we're thinking of facts about stars. Coby: Hey! I know!
Stars are— Miss Gray: Let's give
someone else a chance, Coby. Coby: Sorry. It's
just that I love stars! Miss Gray: Okay,
boys and girls. Please sit down.
Coby: Miss Gray!
Now are you going to tell us about seeing stars? Please? Mark: Look,
Coby! I'm already seeing stars! That means
I'm dizzy! Coby: Mark!
Shh! Miss
Gray: Room Two is going to see stars at the . . . Coby:
Mom! Guess what! My class is going to see stars!
Mrs. Rock: What?
Coby: We're going to the space museum!
Coby: The space museum is going to be so fun!
We're going to watch a show inside a huge globe!
Mrs. Rock: The space museum!
Coby: Here's my permission slip.
You have to sign it, or I can't go.
Mrs. Rock: I'll do that right now.
Mark: Hey, Coby! Want to play basketball?
Coby: Sure! I'll be on your
team! Mark: Okay. It's you and me against Juan and
Billy. Miss Gray: Good morning, boys and
girls. Today is a big day for Room Two!
Class: Yeah!
Eve: We're going on a field trip!
We're going on a field
trip! Miss Gray: But some of you still haven’t given me your permission
slips. Hmm . . . Kara, Coby, and Juan.
Kara: Here's mine.
Juan: And mine.
Coby: It's in here somewhere . . .
I know my mom signed it.
Miss Gray: Coby? Do you have
yours? Mark: I'll help you look,
Coby. Jenna: Oh dear . . . I'm filled with
fear. Did Coby lose his permission
slip? Coby: Miss Gray, I can't find it
anywhere. Miss Gray: That's too bad,
Coby. Coby: Can I still go to the
space museum? Miss Gray: Not without a signed permission
slip, Coby. That's the rule at South
Street. Coby: But . . . But . . . Can we call my mom to get
permission? Miss Gray: No, Coby,
I'm sorry. You'll have to stay here—in the principal's office.
Coby: Have fun at the space museum.
Mark: Sorry you can’t come with
us. Kara: That's what happens when you forget your permission
slip. Daisy: That was mean,
Kara! Kara:
Sorry. Miss Gray: Coby, bring a book
with you. And
your homework. Mr. Lenny:
Hi, Coby. Coby: Hi,
Mr. Lenny. Mr. Lenny: What are you doing here in
Mr. Miller’s office? Coby: I lost
my permission slip. So I couldn't go on
the field trip. And the space museum is my
favorite place. Mr. Lenny: Oh. That's
too bad. Coby: My class is going to see a star show and
learn about planets. And I'm stuck here, missing all
the fun. Mr. Lenny: Hmm . . . Maybe not
all the fun. Coby: What
do you mean? Mr. Lenny: I have an
idea . . . Miss Gray: Room Two,
please take a seat. The star show starts in
three minutes. Mark: Cool! The ceiling is shaped
like a globe. Miss
Gray: That's right. The ceiling is supposed to look like the
night sky. Shh, everyone!
Kids: Ooh! Whoa . . .
Mark: Look! There's the Milky Way! And
Saturn! Mark: Too bad Coby missed the star
show. Jenna: I know. Poor
Coby. He's probably so bored right now.
Mark:
Yep. Mr. Lenny: Ready,
helper? Coby: I'm ready, Mr.
Lenny! Mr. Lenny: Then let's
go. Our first job is to fix the slide on the playground . . .
Mr. Lenny: We’re going to tighten some bolts.
Coby: Hey . . . What's Mr. Miller
doing? Mr. Lenny: He's telling Mandy to take her dog
home. No dogs allowed at school.
Coby: What's our next job, Mr. Lenny?
Mr. Lenny: We have to sweep the art room floor.
Coby: Okay. This is
fun! Coby: Look! Now Mr. Miller is visiting
kindergarten. Mr. Miller: That’s it for me,
kids. I’m
exhausted. Coby: Wow, the principal has a
hard job! Miss Gray: Who knows what planet
this is? Mark: Coby would know if
he were here. Daisy: It’s red, so I
think it’s Mars. Miss Gray: Right, Daisy. Mars is called
the red planet. On Mars the sky
looks pink. Kara: Pink! That’s my
favorite color! Mark: Where are we
going next? Miss Gray:
The gift shop. Mark: Oh good. I brought money
to buy something. Mr. Lenny: This is our last
job—cleaning the principal’s windows. Oh . . .
That’s odd. Coby: Yeah. Why are the
lights off? Wow! This is
amazing! Mr. Miller: It’s been a
hard day. So I’m relaxing under
the stars. But don't tell anyone!
Coby: It’s awesome! I can see the Big
Dipper! Mark: Coby! We’re
back. Sorry you missed the star show. But
look. I brought you something from the gift
shop. Was it really boring here?
Coby: Umm . . . Well, I did get to be Mr. Lenny’s
helper. And that was fun!
Daisy: Miss Gray, is Picture Day coming soon?
Miss Gray: Yes. It's next week, Daisy.
Daisy: Finally!
Mark: Who cares about Picture
Day? Daisy: Me! I love Picture
Day. Mark: Why? All we do is stand there and smile at the
camera. Coby: Yeah. It's sooo
boring! Daisy: Well, I want to be a rock star one day. Or a
dancer. So I like to get my picture
taken. Kara: I like Picture Day too,
Daisy. Daisy:
Oh. Kara: Because my mom always buys me a pretty new
dress. Coby: My mom gets me a new dress
too! Mark: Ha-ha! Come on,
Coby. Let's practice getting our picture taken!
Coby and Mark:
Cheese! Daisy: Very funny, you
two. Just don't make those silly faces on the real Picture Day.
Jenna: Yeah! That will ruin our class picture.
Daisy: Guess what, Mom! Picture Day is coming soon.
Mrs. Gomez: Oh, good. We'll have new pictures to send to your
grandparents. Daisy: Can I get a new dress?
Please? Mrs. Gomez: I'm sorry,
Daisy. A new dress costs too
much. Daisy: Oh . . . That's okay . .
. Mrs. Gomez: But we can borrow your cousin's blue
dress. And we'll get new ribbons for your hair too.
Daisy: Great idea, Mom.
I'll be so beautiful, I won't need a new dress!
Mrs. Gomez: Right!
Jenna: Daisy, I like your dress.
Daisy: Thank you. I borrowed it from my
cousin. Jenna: I have on my favorite shirt for Picture
Day. Daisy: Yay! The purple
one! Jenna: You look nice,
Mark. Mark: Thanks. I'm wearing my
monster tie. It makes me walk like a
monster! Jenna and Daisy:
Ah! Jenna: Ugh. Look who's
coming. Daisy: Oh no.
It's Kara. She's going to show off her new
clothes. Kara: Hi, Daisy! Hi,
Jenna! Do you notice anything different about
me? Daisy: Um . . .
No. Jenna: Me
neither. Come on, Daisy. Let's go line up.
Miss Gray: We're getting our pictures taken
soon. But first we have a treat. Mark:
Yes! A treat! Jim:
What is it? Coby:
Please, oh please. Let it be an extra recess.
Miss Gray: Sorry, Coby. It's not an extra recess.
But it's something good—today is Maya's birthday. Maya:
Yep. It's my birthday. So
I brought in muffins and juice for everyone. Class: Happy
Birthday, Maya! Maya: Thank
you. Mark? Can you please help me give out the treats? Mark:
Sure. Monster Mark is at your service. Jim:
Yum. Berry juice! Daisy:
Thanks for the muffin, Maya.
Mark: One berry juice coming right up, Daisy. Whoops!
Daisy: Oh no! Mark!
Mark: I'm so sorry, Daisy!
Daisy: My dress! My cousin is going to be so mad at
me! Miss Gray: I'm sorry that happened,
Daisy. Mark, you should not have been walking like a monster! Mark:
I know. I'm sorry. Miss
Gray: The school nurse will help you get cleaned up.
Maybe your mom can bring you some new clothes. Daisy: She's
working today. Miss Gray:
Well, the nurse will have dry clothes for you. Daisy: But
. . . But . . . It's Picture Day. Miss
Gray: I know, honey. It's a shame. School
Nurse: Here you go, Daisy.
These clothes should fit you.
Daisy: Thank you.
Jenna: You still look pretty, Daisy.
Daisy: No, I don't.
I don't like orange and I don't like teddy
bears. Why, oh why, did this have to happen today?
Photographer: Miss Gray's class, you're next!
Mark: Don't worry, Daisy.
Coby and I won't make any silly faces. We promise. Coby:
Yeah. Our class picture is going to be great!
Kara: Yuck. Didn't the nurse have any nice clothes?
Daisy: No.
Photographer: On the count of three, everybody say "Cheese!"
One . . . Two . . . Kara:
You're going to ruin the picture.
Daisy: No, I'm not! I can't help it if—
Photographer: Three!
Class: Cheese!
Miss Gray: Our pictures are here, class.
Daisy:
Uh-oh. Mark: How does our class picture
look? Miss Gray: Um . .
. Coby:
Oh boy. Maya:
Not good. Eve: I really wanted a nice
class picture. Jim:
Me too. Daisy: It's my
fault. And Kara's. Kara: I
didn't do anything. Daisy: Yes, you did. You were saying
mean things to me! Kara: Well, you should
blame Mark, not me. He's the one who
spilled juice on you! Miss Gray:
Okay, girls, that's enough. Class, please put
the pictures away. It's time to go
home. Daisy: Your dad is the best at cleaning
clothes, Jenna. Jenna: That's why he owns a laundry
business, I guess. I'm glad all the juice stains
came out. Daisy:
Me too. Jenna: But why did Miss Gray tell us to wear our Picture
Day clothes again?
Daisy: I don't know. Look! Monster
Mark is back. Ah! Don't come
near me! Miss Gray: I have
good news, class. It's Picture Day
again. Class:
What? Daisy: What do you mean,
Miss Gray? Miss Gray: The photographer is coming back at
ten o'clock. He's going to take our picture
again. Maybe this one will come out better.
Class: Hooray!
Daisy: I won't make a mean face this time.
Kara: Me neither.
Photographer: Okay, Room
Two. On the count of three, say "Cheese."
One . . . Two . . . Three!
Class: Cheese!
Miss Gray: The school science fair is next month.
And you know how I feel about science! Jenna: How,
Miss Gray? Miss
Gray: I love it! Mark:
Why do you love science? Miss
Gray: Because it helps us learn about plants and— Coby:
Space! Jenna:
And weather! Juan:
And animals! Miss
Gray: Right! Science is about all of those things. And
I know everyone in this class will make great projects. Mark: Coby,
what's your science fair project? Coby: I'm
going to count stars in the night sky. Mark: That's
a good idea. Kara: I'm
studying caterpillars. Mark: What
about them? Kara: How
they turn into beautiful butterflies. Jenna:
I'm making a tornado in a bottle. Maya:
Me too! Daisy:
Hey! I'm doing the same project! Coby:
What's your science project, Mark? Mark:
I haven't thought of one yet. Coby:
You're good at science. I'll
bet you'll think of something cool.
Maya: You could make soap bubbles.
Mark: Nah. Bubbles are for babies.
Coby: You could study evaporation.
Mark: Boring!
Jenna: Why don't you ask Miss Gray?
She's got lots of good ideas.
Mark: I know. But I want to surprise her with a really cool
project. Kara: You'd better think of something soon,
Mark. It takes a long time to make a good project.
Coby: Did you think of an idea for the science fair
yet? Mark: Yep. I'm going to watch a
plant. To see how it
grows. Coby: You're going to watch
a plant? Mark: It'll
be cool. Coby: It sounds . . . um . .
. boring.
Mark: Really? Coby: Yeah. But I'm glad you're not making a tornado
in a bottle. Everybody is
making those! Mark: Come on, plant. Don't just
sit there. Grow! Zack:
You look weird. What
are you doing? Mark: I'm working
on my science project. It was fun when
the seed sprouted. But
now it's—
Zack: Boring! Juan: Hi, Mark. Want to come out
and play football? Mark: I can't. I'm working
on my project. I'm watching a
plant grow. Juan: Oh. That sounds . . . uh . .
. fun! Bye. Mark: Coby and
Zack were right.
This project is boring! Hey, guys! Can
I play football? Coby: When are we going to share
our science projects? Miss Gray: The fair is
still weeks away, Coby. We'll share them on the day of
the fair. Maya and Jenna:
I can't wait! Kara: My project
is so great! I'm going to win a ribbon
for sure! Miss Gray: I'm sure everyone will have
a great project. I'm looking forward to . .
. Mark? What's wrong?
Mark: I have a problem—a science fair problem!
Miss Gray: Let's go into the hall, Mark.
Please tell me what's wrong. Mark:
I'm doing my science project on how a plant grows. But
watching a plant is boring—really boring! And
now I don't know what to do. Miss Gray:
You could choose a new project. Mark:
I guess I could do that . . . Miss
Gray: You always have good ideas, Mark.
I'm sure you'll think of something wonderful. Mrs. Conlan:
Are you doing your homework? Mark: I'm
thinking of ideas for a new science project. Zack:
What happened to the plant project? Mark:
You were right. It
was boring.
Zack: Why don't you make a tornado in a bottle?
They're really cool. You
shake them and—
Mark: Yeah, yeah, I know.
Everybody is making those.
Mark: I like plants.
So I want to have a plant
project. But it has to be something cool.
Mrs. Conlan: Hmm . . .
Mr. Conlan: Zack! Are you ready? Come
on. It's time for your basketball game! Zack:
Oh no. He's got his cameras again.
Mrs. Conlan: You boys are growing up so fast.
Your father loves taking pictures of you. Mark:
That's it! I've got a great idea! Mrs.
Conlan: Where are you going, Mark? Mark:
Hey, Dad! When you get back, can I borrow your video camera?
Kara: Hi, Mark! Hi, Coby!
Want to see my project again?
It's about butterflies.
Mark and Coby: No, thanks.
Mark: Wow! Are those raisins?
Juan: Yes. I mixed vinegar with baking soda to make them
swim. Coby:
Cool! Mrs. Conlan: Mark, the judges are going to your
table. You'd better get over there. Mark:
The best projects win ribbons.
I hope I win one! Judge
1: What's your project, young man? Mark:
I studied how plants grow. And
I made a movie about it. Judge
2: You made a movie? May
we see it? Mark:
Sure! Judge
1: Hmm. Judge
Judge 1: Your project is very unusual. Thank you.
Zack: Now what?
Mrs. Conlan: We have to wait for the judges to
decide. Mr. Conlan: Mark, let me take another picture of
you. Stand right there, in front of your plant again! Mrs.
Conlan: What are those?
Mark: Tornados in a bottle.
Mr. Conlan: I see they were popular this year.
Mark: That's for sure.
Mr. Miller: Thank you for coming to the science
fair. We had some great projects this year. Soon
we'll be giving out ribbons for the best ones. Mark: I
hope mine wins. Mr. Miller:
But first, we'd like to show you a project. Man: Show
us? What is he talking about? Mr.
Miller: Lights, please! Crowd:
Amazing! Wow! Miss
Gray: Nice job, Mark! You
won a ribbon! Mark:
Thanks, Miss Gray.
Miss Gray: I just love science, don't you?
Mark: Yes!
Mr. Miller: Good morning, Room Two!
Class: Good morning, Mr. Miller!
Mr. Miller: I'm here to tell you about the Superstar Reading Contest.
Juan: What's
that? Miss Gray:
Shh. Mr. Miller: I'm asking Room Two to read, read,
read! Jim: I don't like to
read. Jenna: You don't like to
read? I love to
read. Miss Gray: Jim. Jenna. Please
listen. Mr. Miller: Room Two must read one hundred books
this month. If you do, I'll celebrate by doing something wacky.
Mark: Like what, Mr. Miller?
Mr. Miller: I'll shave off all my hair!
Coby: But you're bald!
Kids: Ha-ha!
Mr. Miller: I'll surprise you with something wacky, I promise.
Kids: Woo-hoo! Hooray!
Jenna: No problem, Mr.
Miller. We can do
it! Jenna: Dad, can you take me to the
library? Mr. Gibson: Sure. What
for? Jenna: Mr. Miller wants our class to read one hundred
books. If we do, he'll do something wacky.
Mr. Gibson: That sounds like a big
challenge. Jenna: Nope. I can probably read one hundred books all by
myself. Mr. Gibson: You do love to
read! Mrs. Gibson: Did you find good books at the
library? Jenna:
Yes! Mrs. Gibson: Wow. But they're all thick chapter books,
honey. Are you sure you can read them in a month?
Jenna: Yep, I'm sure.
When it comes to reading, I'm already a superstar!
Coby: Do we have any homework?
Mark: It's Friday. And we don't get homework on
weekends. Right, Miss Gray?
Miss Gray: Actually, Mark, I am giving you homework this weekend.
Class: Oh no.
Miss Gray: Everyone has to read, read,
read! Mark: Oh, right, the Superstar Reading
Contest. Coby: Don't worry, Miss
Gray. We can do
it. And we have Jenna in our class.
Class: Yay, Jenna!
Mrs. Gibson: You've got a busy day,
Jenna. Your soccer game is at ten. And
Ella's pool party starts at three. Jenna: Mmm-hmm .
. . Coach: Jenna!
Jenna: Sorry.
We're having a reading contest at school. And I'm
still reading my first book. Coach: Well, the
game starts in two minutes. Mr. Gibson:
Shoot, Jenna! Mrs. Gibson:
Good try, honey! Coach: Come
on, girls! Play hard out there! Mrs. Gibson:
Jenna's running a lot today. Mr. Gibson:
Two players are sick today. So
the other girls have to play extra hard. Mrs. Gibson: Happy
Birthday, Ella. Ella: Thanks, Mrs.
Gibson. Come in the
pool, Jenna! Mrs. Gibson:
Remember the rules, Jenna. No reading
in the pool! Daisy: Ella's
pool party was fun, wasn't it? Jenna: Yeah.
The best part was the slide. Daisy:
I know. We went down it about fifty times! Mr.
Gibson: Where's Jenna? Mrs.
Gibson: In her room, reading. Mr.
Gibson: Wow . . . I bet our reading superstar is on her third or fourth book by now.
Kids: Hi, Mr. Miller.
Mr. Miller: Hi, kids. Is it time for recess?
Daisy: Yes. Do you know what our reading prize is
yet? Coby: Remember, Mr. Miller, you promised to do something
wacky! Mr. Miller: Only if Room Two reads one hundred
books. Daisy: We will. We have Jenna in
our class! Coby: Do you know what you're going to
do yet? Mr. Miller: I have a
few ideas. I might let someone throw a pie in my
face. Mark: Ooh! Can I do
it? Daisy: What are your other
ideas? Mr. Miller: I might dance on the school
roof. Or eat some worms.
Kara: Yuck!
Mr. Miller: Whatever it is, it will be wacky.
I promise. Bye, kids.
Mark: I can't wait to see what he
does. Coby: It's going to be
great. Kara: Everybody had better be
reading! Daisy: Let's check the chart after
lunch. Come on, Jenna! It's jump-rope time!
Mark: I read five books so
far. Coby: I read
six. Kara: I finished my tenth book this
morning. That's more than anyone else in the class.
Daisy: I don't think so,
Kara. Jenna's probably read way more books than you.
Kara: No, she hasn't, Daisy.
Look at the chart!
Mark: Uh-oh.
Coby: Oh boy. Jenna!
Jenna: Kara's right. I haven't even read one book
yet. If we lose, it'll be all my fault!
Daisy: What happened, Jenna?
Jenna: The problem is that I like chapter books.
Really long chapter books! Mark:
You'll catch up.
Daisy: You can do it, Jenna.
You're a reading superstar!
Jenna: Dad, can you take me to the library?
Mr. Gibson: Did you finish all those chapter books?
Jenna: I finished one of them.
Now I need some more books—Shorter ones!
Mrs. Gibson: Lights out, honey.
Jenna: In a minute, Mom.
Mr. Gibson: Jenna! Daisy's here.
Time for school.
Jenna: Coming!
